title: Yisroel: the mind growing up inside the middos, from nursing to Keser Chabad
overview:
The chapter turns to *Zeir Anpin*, which is called Yisroel and Yaakov, and asks what the name Yisroel means: the *middos* run by the *sechel*, the Name *MaH* of *chachma* sorting out and ruling over *BaN*, *Elokim*. Its source is *Yisroel Saba*, the *middos* within *chachma*; the *middos* below it, born from the drop of *Abba*, are *Yisroel Zuta*.

Rabbi Markel teaches the rest as a child growing up. When a *midda* is born the reasons leave and only the outline stays: an angry man knows only that this is a bad guy. The newborn *middos* are an embryo, only stamped by the outside of the *sechel*. Through nursing, to six, they become ready for *mochin*; from six to nine the mind of *bina* gives conduct by reason, which a dog can never have; at nine *chachma* comes in and he thinks for himself. From thirteen to twenty comes *Keser Chabad*, the power to change the will itself, as the Rebbeim's limbs did the *halacha* by themselves. That master of his own nature is Yisroel, and most people, he says, never get past nine.

sections.title: Yisroel: the middos of chachma, Yisroel Saba and Yisroel Zuta
sections.summary: *Zeir Anpin* has two levels, Yisroel and Yaakov. Yisroel is the *middos* according to *sechel*: the Name *MaH* of *chachma* sorting out *BaN*. Its source is *Yisroel Saba*, the *middos* within *chachma*; the *middos* below *chachma*, drawn from the drop of *Abba*, are *Yisroel Zuta*.

phrases.he: (לד) והנה בבחינת זעיר אנפין דאצילות יש ב' מדריגות הנקרא ישראל ויעקב כידוע
וביאור פרטי המדריגות שבזה.
הנה תחלה יש להבין בטעם קריאת שם ישראל, כי שרית עם אלהי״ם כו'
והוא שם מ''ה שמברר ושולט על שם ב''ן כו', כי בחכמה אתברירו וכח הדכר לברר כו' האיש דרכו לכבוש כו'

blocks.text: *Zeir Anpin* (the small countenance) of *Atzilus* has two levels, called Yisroel and Yaakov. First, why the name Yisroel, "for you have striven with *Elokim*"? It is the Name *MaH* (the Name of forty-five) that sorts out and rules over the Name *BaN*, for "in *chachma* (wisdom) they are sorted out", and "the way of a man is to conquer". In other words, Yisroel is the *middos* (emotional attributes) according to *sechel* (intellect).

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים, הנה תחלה יש להבין ההפרש בין ישראל סבא לישראל זוטא
שבחינת המדות שבחכמה עצמה נקרא ישראל סבא
ויש בזה ב' מדריגות, הא' מדות שבאור אבא, והב' מדות שבחכמה סתימאה
והוא הנקרא אדם קדמאה בלשון הזהר
וזה שכתוב מה שמו מה שם בנו כו'

blocks.text:
*Yisroel Saba* (lit. Israel the elder) is the *middos* within *chachma*, on two levels: in the light of *Abba*, and, inside, in *chachma stima'a* (hidden *chachma*). The *Zohar* calls it *Adam Kadma'a*; not *Adam Kadmon*, but the upper *Yisroel Saba*.

"What is His name and what is His son's name" was applied earlier to *Arich* and *Zeir Anpin*. Here it is the same in detail: how the *middos* of *chachma* come into *Zeir Anpin* when it is called Yisroel, not Yaakov.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: On the second reading: "what is His name and what is His son's name" seems here to speak of *Yisroel Saba* in *chachma stima'a* and *Yisroel Saba* in *chachma*. But it applies as well to *Yisroel Saba* in *chachma* and *Yisroel Zuta*.

phrases.he: ובחינת המדות שלמטה מן החכמה נקרא ישראל זוטא, כי הם בבחינת קטנות
לאחר שהן באין בבחינת הצמצום, והעלם עיקר עצם השכל
רק מה שהכלי חיצוניות דנצח והוד דאבא ממשיך להוליד ולהמציא שכל לחסד ואהבה, נקרא חסד זוטא כו'
(וכמשל טיפה במוח האב כו', כך נאמר מה שם בנו שהוא ישראל זוטא, שנמשך לו מטיפת אבא כו' וכידוע)

blocks.text: The *middos* below *chachma* are *Yisroel Zuta* (the small Israel), in *katnus* (smallness): the essence of the *sechel* is hidden, and only what the outer vessel of *netzach* and *hod* of *Abba* draws down gives birth to a *sechel* for love. This was explained from chapter 25 on, with the three levels in *chachma*. The son comes from the drop of *Abba*, and that drop holds two things: *Yisroel Saba* in *chachma* itself and *Yisroel Saba* in *chachma stima'a*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

sections.title: When the midda is born, the reasons of Ima leave and the overview of Abba stays
sections.summary: The reasons come to the *middos* through *Nehi* of *Ima*, and they leave at the moment the *midda* is aroused; the outline that comes from *Nehi* of *Abba* stays. Before the birth the love is hidden in the reasoning like a fetus in the womb.

phrases.he: והנה מבחינת נה''י דאבא נמשך בנה''י דאימא
שהוא בחינת השפעת והשפלת השגה וטעם למדת החסד כו'
אך בחינת נה''י דאימא מסתלקין בשעת תולדת גלוי התפעלות מדת האהבה וכהאי גוונא
כנראה בחוש
שמתקצר ומסתלק הטעם והשכל בשעת התפעלות המדה
phrases.en: The actual logical *taam* and the whole *hisbonenus* goes away at the time that the *midda* is *mispael*

blocks.text: From *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*) of *Abba* it is drawn into *Nehi* of *Ima* (*bina* as a *partzuf*), which brings the grasp and the reason down to the *middos*. But when the love is aroused, the *Nehi* of *Ima* depart: **the actual logical *taam* and the whole *hisbonenus* goes away at the time that the *midda* is *mispael***. Not the *Nehi* of *Abba*: the outside of the overview of the thing does get through.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.title: Why are you mad?
blocks.text: Ask a man why he is mad while he is actually mad. Later he could go back and think through all the *pratim* (details), but while he is mad they fade away, even their outside. To tell you what the other man did, he would have to stop and think about it, and stop being mad. The *klal* (the general idea) is there: "What do you mean, why am I mad? This is a bad guy who did a bad thing to me." That is only the very outside of the *klal*. The *Nehi* of *Ima* is gone; the *Nehi* of *Abba* is still there.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: On the second reading he adds that this goes *davka* (precisely) through *tevuna*, *Ima tata'a* (the lower mother), and ties it to what is said in chapter 2.

phrases.he: (והוא ענין וראיתן על האבנים כו',
שהירכים מצטננות
phrases.en: in women their thighs, their legs get cold

phrases.he: בשעת לידה
שנסתלקו נה''י הראשונים ונמשכים נה''י חדשים כו'
phrases.en: the first *Nehi* of *bina* are gone, and the second *Nehi*, *d'gufa d'Zeir Anpin*, comes through

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)
ונקרא בחינת בקיעת יסוד דאימא
phrases.en: It goes through *yesod* of *Ima*, the connection of *bina* into the *middos*; you have to sort of break through it

phrases.he: להוליד המדה
ותחלה כלולה האהבה בהעלם מכוסה בשכל,
phrases.en: originally the love and the fear is actually included in the logic, but it's totally hidden

phrases.he: כעובר במעי אמו כו'

blocks.text: This is why, in the body, **in women their thighs, their legs get cold** in childbirth, and they are given hot blankets: the first *Nehi*, of *bina*, are gone, and the second, of the body of *Zeir Anpin*, come through. It is called the breaking of *yesod* of *Ima*, the connection of *bina* into the *middos*: it has to be broken through to give birth to the *midda*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: At first the love or the fear is included in the logic, in the details and reasoning of the thing, **but it's totally hidden**, like a fetus in its mother's womb.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: On the second reading: what goes over is just a *bechina* (an aspect), not the real outside of the actual *sechel* but an outside of an outside. And in the intellect the *midda* is inherent.

sections.title: Three levels of mind in the middos, and the middos as an embryo
sections.summary: Once born, the *middos* grow through three levels of *mochin*: nursing, the first maturity of *Ima* and the second of *Abba*, at six, nine, thirteen and twenty. At the start they are three within three, like an embryo: only the outside of *Nehi* reaches them, a stamp of the *sechel*.

phrases.he: אבל לאחר שנולדו המדות
הרי הם כלולים מחסדים דאבא וגבורות דאימא בכללות ופרטות שלהם
phrases.en: And then they're made up from the *chassadim* of *Abba* and *gevuros* of *Ima*, in general and in particular

phrases.he: הרי יש ג' מדריגות: בחינת מוחין דיניקה ובחינת מוחין דגדלות ראשון דאימא וגדלות שני דאבא כו' כידוע.

blocks.text: Once the *middos* are born, they are **made up from the *chassadim* of *Abba* and *gevuros* of *Ima***. There are three levels: *mochin d'yenika* (the mind of nursing), the *gadlus rishon d'Ima* (the first maturity, of *Ima*) and the *gadlus sheni d'Abba* (the second, of *Abba*). Later the text gives four: in *Abba* there is also its inside, which includes the inside of *Ima*, all from the inner *Yisroel Saba*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: It is a whole big *inyan*. The basic levels are at six, nine, thirteen and twenty years old, and each breaks down further. Not that at six, poof, he has it: from one to six is *mochin d'yenika*; from six to nine the second process starts; from nine to thirteen the *mochin* of *Abba* start, and at thirteen he is considered to have them, which is why he is *bar mitzva*. They are not fully in yet, only as far as *Chabad*. Only at twenty is it called *Keser Chabad*, and then he can buy and sell in his father's property. To really go through it would take more than another ten minutes.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: On the second reading he notes that the "etc." after the three levels means there is a fourth.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים, בהיות ידוע שהמדות הם בבחינת עיבור
תלת גו תלת כו'
phrases.en: *Chabad* inside of *Chagas* and *Chagas* inside of *Nehi*

phrases.he: דהיינו רק חיצוניות נה''י, ובהם כלול בהעלם חב''ד וחג''ת כו'
phrases.en: the only *mochin* that's in the *middos* is in *Nehi*, and even that's a *chitzoniyus* of *Nehi*, but hidden inside of it is really the whole *sechel*

blocks.text: The *middos* are in *ibur* (gestation), three within three: ***Chabad* inside of *Chagas* and *Chagas* inside of *Nehi***. So lies a fetus in its mother, in the fetal position, its head between its knees: the *Chabad* is in the *Nehi*.

Even though all that comes over to the *middos* is a *bechina*, hidden in it is the whole *sechel*. The only *mochin* in the *middos* is in *Nehi*, and not just *Nehi*: *mamash* (literally) the *chitzoniyus* (the outside) of *Nehi*. Yet inside it is really the whole *sechel*.

phrases.he: והוא רק בחינת טבעיות המדות כו'

blocks.text: *Tivius hamiddos*, the nature of the *middos*: *teva* is like *matbe'a*, a stamp, and like *tov'u*, "they drowned": sinking in. It is what sinks in, what is stamped in. A listener offers "embedded"; he is not sure what word to use, but he likes "stamp".

blocks.title: The stamp on the back of a check
blocks.text: The *midda* is just stamped over from the *sechel*, and only the very outside of the *sechel*, the final conclusion: I like him or I don't like him. Later the book speaks of an engraved seal, things stamped over and over from one level to the next. The first books were printed like that, with letters, and people stamp the back of a check instead of signing it; the stamp has letters that stick out. So the letters of the *sechel* stick out, only the letters of *Nehi*, and they stamp the *midda*. All a *midda* of *katnus* knows is: I'm happy, I'm sad, I like him, I hate him. That is *tivius hamiddos*.

sections.title: Nursing to six: the natural midda, then conduct by reason
sections.summary: Through nursing the *middos* grow ready for *mochin*. A baby has only the stamped, natural *midda*, with a mind in great *tzimtzum*; at six there is enough *sechel* to explain things and expect conduct, unlike an animal that can only be trained.

phrases.he: וביניקה מתגדלים להיות בהכנה לקבל מוחין,
phrases.en: With *yenika* they grow to become just prepared to receive some *mochin*

phrases.he: והוא כמו התינוק שמתגדלים אבריו מיניקת חלב אמו כידוע
עד שבהיותו בן ו' שנה
phrases.en: Until he's six years old

phrases.he: יש במדותיו מוחין בצמצום

blocks.text: **With *yenika* they grow to become just prepared to receive some *mochin*** (a listener corrects the reading to *b'hachana*, "prepared"). The *midda* will not just follow its nature and get mad at once: he will think before he acts, and finally be able to think before the *midda* even takes shape.

blocks.title: The baby and the toy
blocks.text: Like a baby whose limbs grow from his mother's milk. A little baby has an instant, natural *midda*; natural or stamped is no contradiction, in Hebrew it is the same word. When he's hungry he shouts. Say goochie-goochie and he laughs; talk to him and he's happy. Another kid takes his toy and he gets mad. That is as far as the *sechel* goes.

Still, there has to be a *sechel*. He understands that he wanted the toy and the other kid took it, so he's mad: a logical *havana*. And *chachma*, higher than logic, holds the whole incident in his mind; memory, as it says, is from *chachma*. After a few times he will hate that kid before he takes the toy. That is not an analysis of today's case but an overview: I know this guy.

blocks.title: The lollipop
blocks.text: But the mind is in a very big *tzimtzum* (contraction): all it awakens is the natural *midda* already there. If he wants a lollipop and you don't give it to him, he gets mad, and you can't tell him it's bad for his teeth; there isn't enough *sechel* for that. **Until he's six years old**: that is why kids start school around six, because by then there are *mochin* in his *middos*, in *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: אך בבחינת הטעם ושכל לנהוג בכל דרכיו,
לא מדות טבעיות כבהמה לבד כו'
phrases.en: not just natural *middos* like a *behema*

blocks.title: The dog and the carpet
blocks.text: At six you can already explain to him that he shouldn't piss on the carpet. A dog you can't explain it to: he doesn't do it because you'll hit him. That is training; you never explained that the carpet will get ruined. You can teach a dog not to attack certain people because they are our friends, but that is not an explanation: his *middos* themselves are handled with love and fear. He sees you love this man, so he loves him; he knows you'll get mad, so he doesn't do it, without understanding why. A six-year-old can already be given certain reasons, but it is not a real *sechel*, only a *sechel* for the *middos* themselves.

sensitivity.reason: Uses a coarse word for a child or a dog relieving himself.
sensitivity.publishable: At six you can already explain to him that he shouldn't wet the carpet. A dog you can't explain it to: he doesn't do it because you'll hit him. That is training; you never explained that the carpet will get ruined. You can teach a dog not to attack certain people because they are our friends, but that is not an explanation: his *middos* themselves are handled with love and fear. He sees you love this man, so he loves him; he knows you'll get mad, so he doesn't do it, without understanding why. A six-year-old can already be given certain reasons, but it is not a real *sechel*, only a *sechel* for the *middos* themselves.

blocks.text: Reason and *sechel* only to conduct himself: a *hanhaga*. He asks for the English word and a listener gives it: conduct. You can already expect a certain conduct from him, **not just natural *middos* like a *behema*** (an animal).

sections.title: Nine: fit to give birth to thoughts of his own
sections.summary: From six to nine the mind of *bina* grows; at nine *chachma* comes in and he can think for himself what it is all about, and the *midda* itself can start to come from the *sechel*. The ages are a process, and most people never get far along it.

phrases.he: עד היותו בן ט'
phrases.en: at the time that he's nine years old

phrases.he: שאז ראוי להוליד
phrases.en: *ra'uy l'holid* new *machshavos* on his own

phrases.he: שאז הוא בחינת גדלות המוחין יותר,
דהיינו יותר מכפי המצטרך אל המדות לבד
phrases.en: it's already more than just an analysis of what the *middos* need

blocks.text: Until nine, when he is *ra'uy l'holid* (fit to give birth), with a greater *gadlus hamochin* (maturity of mind). From six to nine is the *gadlus rishon d'Ima*: it goes by explanation. You explain to him that if everybody goes around hitting everybody, they'll hit you back. That is pure *bina*. From six to nine the *mochin* of *bina* grow, and at nine *chachma* kicks in: **it's already more than just an analysis of what the *middos* need**. He can start to think what it's all about, matters of *chachma*.

The ages are general. Some children can do it at six: *Avraham Avinu* started at three to think about what's going on in the world, because he had a *gadlus hamochin* beyond a normal person. And it is a process. It is not that today is his sixth birthday and, poof, he has *mochin* of *bina*.

And there are people seventy years old who never got to six. They're like a *behema*, with the natural *mochin* of an animal. Others' whole mind for conduct is how to get their way: they're nice to people not because they understand there is such a thing as niceness, but because they want to sell a product.

sensitivity.reason: Says some old people are like an animal, and that some are nice to others only to sell a product.
sensitivity.publishable: And there are people seventy years old who never got to six, with only natural *mochin*. Others' whole mind for conduct is how to get their way: they're nice to people not because they understand there is such a thing as niceness, but because it serves them.

blocks.text: So the ages are not exact: an older person may reach only six or nine, a younger one what the text calls twenty. And what it calls twenty you won't find in 99.9% of people; in most the most is nine, where one starts to think what it's all about. The text speaks of the ideal, a child growing up in a *frum* family studying Torah properly. In our world most people are somewhere between six and nine, maybe even between zero and six. Six means conduct by *sechel*, though only the *sechel* of "this is going to come back and haunt me", what goes around comes around: if I'm mean to people, if I get drunk and beat up my family. A great many people in our world aren't even six by this measure.

sensitivity.reason: Judges that almost nobody reaches the level of twenty, that most people stop at nine or below, and that a great many are not even at six.
sensitivity.publishable: So the ages are not exact: an older person may reach only six or nine, a younger one what the text calls twenty. And what it calls twenty is very rare; most stop at nine, where one starts to think what it's all about. The text speaks of the ideal, a child growing up in a *frum* family studying Torah properly. Six means conduct by *sechel*, though only the *sechel* of "this is going to come back and haunt me", what goes around comes around: if I'm mean to people, if I get drunk and beat up my family.

blocks.question: If hardly anyone gets past nine, how come everybody becomes bar mitzva at thirteen?
blocks.text: Up to thirteen you won't find too many. But they do have the ability: the vessels of their brains do grow up. They just don't have the emotional maturity.

So at nine he is ***ra'uy l'holid* new *machshavos* on his own** (thoughts). Not only that his mother and father told him it's not nice to act like that: he thinks for himself what is really proper, more than he needs for the *middos*.

phrases.he: וגם יוכל להיות התחלת התהוות המדה רק מצד השכל והטעם,
וכשיחייב השכל להיפך יולד מדה הפכית,
עד שמדותיו רק על פי השכל
phrases.en: until his *middos* are only according to what the *sechel* is *mechayev*

phrases.he: מה שאין כן קודם לבן ט' אין בו מוחין,
רק לפי המדה
phrases.en: only according to the *midda* itself

phrases.he: שכבר מוטבע בו, שיוכל להתחכם בזה
שזה ימצא גם בחיות ובהמות, התחכמות במדתם למצוא טרף ומזון,
רק שבאדם נקרא חי שבמדבר כו'
phrases.en: it's called the animal within an actual person

phrases.he: ודי למבין.

blocks.text: And the *midda* itself can begin to come from the *sechel*. Before, at six, the *midda* is not according to the *sechel* and reason; only the action is. He does not stop being mad because it's not nice to be mad. He is still mad, but he knows that if you hit there might be problems, and if you rob a bank you'll get arrested. Here the *midda* itself can come into being from the *sechel*, when the *sechel* obliges him to love, or the opposite.

The next side picks up the line: **until his *middos* are only according to what the *sechel* is *mechayev*** (obliges). So six is the end of *mochin d'yenika*; from six to nine he goes into the *mochin* of *Ima*; at nine he has them and starts into the *mochin* of *Abba*, where the *middos* can follow logic, what the *sechel* obliges.

Before nine he has no *mochin* except **according to the *midda* itself**, already stamped into him, and he can be clever within it. Animals have this too: a dog can be clever within its *midda*, cunning in finding prey and food, and animals can learn to act within human society. In a person, **it's called the animal within an actual person**.

sections.title: From nine, nine sefiros in each midda
sections.summary: From nine he is ready for the second maturity, of *Abba*, when the *sechel* rules the *middos*. Each *midda* is then made of nine *sefiros*, and once its *Chabad* has grown its *Nehi* can give birth; at six it had only *Chagas* and *Nehi*.

phrases.he: ומבן ט' ואילך מוכן לגדלות שני דאבא
phrases.en: There he's already ready for the second *gadlus d'Abba*

phrases.he: דהיינו שיהיה התגברות השכל על המדות
phrases.en: not just because the *sechel* is *mechayev* from logic, but actually the *sechel* is the main thing

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין כי מראש צורים כו' באריכות)

blocks.text: From nine on **he's already ready for the second *gadlus d'Abba***. He goes over the ages again, checking the text, until they come out straight: from zero to six *mochin d'yenika*; at six he has the *gadlus* of *Ima*, logical control of his actions, and from six to nine is the *gadlus rishon d'Ima*; at nine he has the full *mochin* of *Ima* and is ready for the *gadlus sheni d'Abba*, as the *mochin* of *Abba* start to grow, from nine to thirteen.

That is, the *sechel* overpowers the *middos*: **not just because the *sechel* is *mechayev* from logic, but actually the *sechel* is the main thing**. It is explained at length elsewhere, on "For from the top of the rocks".

phrases.he: ולכך ראוי להוליד,
phrases.en: That's why at that point he's *ra'uy l'holid*

phrases.he: להיות שאז כל מדה כלולה מט׳ ספירות חב''ד חג''ת נה''י
phrases.en: At that point each *midda* is already made of nine *sefiros*

phrases.he: שכאשר נגדלו המוחין דכל מדה בבחינת חב''ד, אז ממילא יש כח בבחינת נה''י להוליד ולד,
כי הא בהא תליא
phrases.en: the *holada* of *Nehi* comes after from the *Chabad*

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב למעלה באות כ''ו באריכות)
ובהיותו בן ו' היה כל מדה כלולה מחג''ת נה''י לבד כו',
שהמוחין מצומצמין מאד, רק לפי צמצום הטבעיות של המדות כו'

blocks.text: **That's why at that point he's *ra'uy l'holid***: each *midda* is already made of nine *sefiros* (the Divine attributes), *Chabad*, *Chagas* and *Nehi*. When the *mochin* of each *midda* have grown into *Chabad*, the *Nehi* automatically have the power to give birth, for one depends on the other: **the *holada* of *Nehi* comes after from the *Chabad***.

At six each *midda* was made only of *Chagas* and *Nehi*: that starts the *gadlus* of *Ima*. *Chagas* is the inside of the *middos*, the actual analysis of what the *midda* should be. At six the analysis is not what it's all about, only what the *midda* should be: the *mochin* are very contracted, only as much as the natural *middos* need.

sections.title: Thirteen to twenty: Keser Chabad changes the will itself
sections.summary: The second maturity of *Abba* comes in full from thirteen to twenty: he can "sell his father's property", own the *chachma* and change the will of the *midda* itself from above the *sechel*. So the Rebbeim learned *Shulchan Aruch* until their limbs did the *halacha*, and *Avraham Avinu* went even past that.

phrases.he: וגדלות שני, היינו מבן י''ג עד ך',
שראוי למכור בנכסי אביו כו'
phrases.en: he's able to sell the *inyan* of *chachma*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת כחב''ד שבכל מדה כו',
והוא בחינת הטיית הרצון בכל מדה, מלמעלה מן השכל של המדה כו'
phrases.en: he can actually change the actual *ratzon*

blocks.text: There is another *gadlus* in *Abba*, beyond the one he is ready for at nine: the real *gadlus sheni* comes later. At nine he has nine *sefiros*; from thirteen to twenty he is fit to sell his father's property: **he's able to sell the *inyan* of *chachma***. He can sell it because he owns the *chachma*, even the *sechel*. It is not just going by *sechel*; it is higher than *sechel*.

That is *Keser Chabad* in each *midda*, the *hataya* (tilting) of the will in each *midda* from above its *sechel*: **he can actually change the actual *ratzon***. Not just change it by *sechel* because the *sechel* obliges, as in *bina*, or because the thing goes by the *sechel* while the will of the *midda* is still the natural *midda* and the *sechel* only rules the heart.
Rabbi Markel has not met too many people who can do this, so few that it is almost impossible for him even to come up with a good example of how it works.

He can change the *midda* itself from one domain to another: that is what it means to sell it. He can sell the inner will itself, as it is in *chachma stima'a*, all the way up to *gulgalta* (the skull), and change the *etzem haratzon* (the essence of the will).

phrases.he: כמו על דרך משל שינויי צירופי האותיות של השכל, שבא מצד שרש ומקור של עומק השכל ממקורו העצמי דוקא
(כמו שכתוב שם במשל חכם מופלג כו')

blocks.text: It is like the changes in the combinations of the letters of the *sechel*, which come from the root and source of the depth of the *sechel*, from its own source; and this applies all over the place. As it says there, in the analogy of the outstanding sage: he can give you the whole thing in different letters, not only in the letters of the explanation. So the *gadlus hamochin* of *Keser Chabad* goes higher than the *sechel*, and there he can change the will.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 44-45 here (202 w802-849), in the middle of explaining line 41; the alignment marks only his rereading of them at w1294.

blocks.title: The Rebbe Rashab washes three times
blocks.text: The Frierdiker Rebbe said, and other Rebbeim said it too, that he learned *Shulchan Aruch* so well that his limbs would do the *mitzva* by themselves. All the Rebbeim are like that, and it goes back to *Avraham Avinu*. The Rebbe Rashab washed his hands three times, holding the cup with a towel. Asked why three times, when it used to be twice, he said: if I do it, it is because it is in the *Shulchan Aruch*, just because that is the *halacha*. The Mechaber in fact says three times. By a Rebbe all you have to do is watch: how he ties his shoes, that is the *halacha*.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 44-45 here (202 w802-849), in the middle of explaining line 41; the alignment marks only his rereading of them at w1294.

blocks.title: Avraham's hand and the knife
blocks.text: So it says of *Avraham Avinu*, "and he sent forth his hand": his hand did not want to, because it knew that was not really what G-d wanted, and he had to force it to take the knife because G-d told him to. That was the great test: he went past even the level where the body does the *halacha* by itself. If G-d tells you, you can go past that too.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 44-45 here (202 w802-849), in the middle of explaining line 41; the alignment marks only his rereading of them at w1294.

blocks.text: So the *middos*, all the way down to *Malchus*, the actual deeds, come from above the *sechel*: the innermost will supplants the natural *middos*, so that this is what he wants to do. Then the lines are read again.

sections.title: Yisroel: a head and a brain, master over his own nature
sections.summary: Yisroel is *Keser Chabad*: the inside of the *middos* coming from the inside of the *sechel*. From the inner *chachma* he sorts out *BaN*, *Elokim*, and is master over his nature, the *tzaddik* who changes the will itself. This speaks of Rebbeim, not of a normal person.

phrases.he: והיינו בחינת ישראל,
phrases.en: that is what *bechinas Yisroel* is

phrases.he: לי ראש ומוחין,
phrases.en: I have a head and a brain

phrases.he: דהיינו בחינת כחב''ד כו'
שאז הוא בחינת גדלות המוחין ביותר, שיוכל לברר לבחינת ב''ן
phrases.en: then he can be *mevarer* the *bechinas BaN*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת אלהי״ם כידוע,
משום דבחכמה, פנימית כח מ''ה דוקא שמבחינת הכתר דחכמה שבמדות כו', אתברירו כו'
phrases.en: the *birurim* don't come from *chitzoniyus hachachma*, it's from *pnimiyus hachachma*

blocks.text: And **that is what *bechinas Yisroel* is**: "*li rosh*", **I have a head and a brain**, *Keser Chabad*. That is what Yisroel means: the inside of the *middos* coming from the inside of the *sechel*.

Then it is the greatest *gadlus hamochin*, and **then he can be *mevarer* the *bechinas BaN*** (sort it out), which is *Elokim*. That is where the *birurim* (sortings) really come from, and why he is master over *Elokim*: master over nature, a total master over his own nature. **The *birurim* don't come from *chitzoniyus hachachma*, it's from *pnimiyus hachachma***.

phrases.he: וכמשל חכם גדול ביותר, שיודע העומק של השכל ממקור הראשון, יודע יותר איך לברר וללבן להוציא הטעות כו'
phrases.en: He is *davka* the guy who knows the *omek hasechel* from the first source; *davka* he can be *mevarer* and *melaben* the *halacha*

phrases.he: וכן חכמתו עמדה לו להתפרנס באומנות או בריוח עבודה כו',
phrases.en: His *chachma* stands for him to do a *parnasa* in *umnus* or *revach avoda*

phrases.he: שנקרא תורתו אומנתו כו'
phrases.en: that his Torah is *mamash* his *umnus*

phrases.he: והיינו ענין האיש דרכו לכבוש כו',
שהוא בחינת שם מ''ה דחכמה שמברר לב''ן כו'
וזה שכתוב כי שרית עם אלהי״ם כו'
phrases.en: that you are master over *Elokim*

phrases.he: ודי למבין:

blocks.text: As with a very great sage: **he is *davka* the guy who knows the *omek hasechel* from the first source** (the depth of the intellect), and *davka* he can sort out and clarify the *halacha*. And his *chachma* stands him in stead to earn a living by a craft, **that his Torah is *mamash* his *umnus***, his craft.
This speaks of someone like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. The whole matter of *Keser Chabad* is Rebbeim, or very, very big people. It is not talking about your normal person.

This is "the way of a man is to conquer", the Name *MaH* of *chachma* sorting out *BaN*; and "for you have striven with *Elokim*": **that you are master over *Elokim***. It is the matter of a *tzaddik*, total master over his nature. As the *Tanya* explains, he does not only stop the *yetzer hara* (the evil inclination), like a *beinoni* (the intermediate man); he changes the initial will itself. Of a *tzaddik* it says, "I hate them with utmost hatred": he hates the evil completely.

Did you read the *Tanya* today? That is what it talks about: the *beinoni*, and that for him it has to come *davka* through *hisbonenus* (contemplation) of the greatness of G-d. That is already obvious.

reviewQuestions.question: While a man is angry, what of his reasons is gone and what is still there? Which *Nehi* is each?
What does *tivius hamiddos* mean, and how does the stamp on the back of a check explain it?
What can you do with a six-year-old that you cannot do with a dog, and why is it still not a real *sechel*?
What changes at nine, when he is *ra'uy l'holid*?
What does it mean to "sell his father's property" at twenty, and how is changing the will itself different from ruling it by *sechel*?
Why is Yisroel "master over *Elokim*", and whom is the chapter really speaking of?
